deep.reconstruction:
Setting (lecture notes of 6.12.1966). f: X -> S, with X_strat the stratifying site (later called the infinitesimal or stratifying site). The previous page showed that a quasi-coherent module F with a stratification relative to S gives a cosimplicial sheaf C^n(F) = lim_i F|Δ^n_{X/S}(i) on X_zar. Here Δ^n_{X/S}(i) is the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{n+1}_S, and F is pulled back along any of the n+1 projections; the stratification makes these pullbacks canonically isomorphic. One then has H^*(X_strat, F) ≅ H^*(X_zar, C^*(F)), a Čech–Alexander description.

This page starts by noting an asymmetry. Stratifying cohomology is a Zariski hypercohomology, of a complex whose differentials are differential operators and so not O-linear. A priori the converse does not seem to hold.

Grothendieck then announces that, roughly, it does hold. To any quasi-coherent F (with no stratification) he attaches a stratified pro-module Q°(F). Comparing with the next page (Q^{i-1}[M] = P^i ⊗_{O_X} M), this is the module of infinitesimal jets P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ F = lim_n P^n_{X/S} ⊗ F. It is stratified through the other factor of the principal parts, and its stratifying cohomology equals the ordinary Zariski cohomology of F.

Q° is functorial for O-linear maps, and also for relative differential operators D: F -> G. An operator of order ≤ n lifts to an O-linear horizontal map of pro-objects, with an index shift; the next page discusses exactly this shift.

Special case: suppose diag: X -> X×_S X is a nilpotent immersion, so P^∞ = O_{X×X}. Then a stratification is the same as a descent datum, and Q°(F) = f^*f_*F. This uses base change, implicitly flat or affine-type hypotheses.

Conclusion of the page: the Zariski hypercohomology of a complex of differential operators (de Rham complex, etc.) can be read as stratifying cohomology of a suitable complex of stratified sheaves. This is the 'linearization of differential operators' trick. Applied to Ω^•, it gives that L(Ω^•) resolves O, and hence H_inf/strat(X/S, O) ≅ H_dR(X/S) in the smooth case.

Purpose: this sets up the comparison between infinitesimal/stratifying cohomology and de Rham cohomology for the 1966–67 crystals lectures.
errors: 'la coh. zariskienne ordinaire de X' should read 'of F': H^*(X_strat, Q°(F)) ≅ H^*(X_zar, F).

The identification of stratifying cohomology of Q°(F) with Zariski cohomology of F needs care with pro-objects and lim^1 / Mittag-Leffler issues. Grothendieck flags this himself with 'à peu de choses près' and the insertion 'plutôt, un pro-Module pro-quasi-cohérent'.
The nilpotent-diagonal formula Q°(F) = f^*f_*F tacitly uses a base change isomorphism p_{1*}p_2^*F ≅ f^*f_*F, which needs hypotheses such as f flat or quasi-compact separated. These are not stated.

ideas.what: Stratifying cohomology as Zariski hypercohomology of the Čech–Alexander complex of jet modules, with non-linear (differential-operator) differentials
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968, notes by Coates–Jussila)

ideas.what: Q°(F) = P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ F as a stratified pro-module whose stratifying cohomology is the Zariski cohomology of F, functorial in differential operators
ideas.modern_name: Linearization functor L (linearization of differential operators)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1968); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974); Berthelot–Ogus (Notes on crystalline cohomology, §6)
ideas.where_published: Probably in the 'Crystals' exposé (infinitesimal site / de Rham comparison); certainly in Berthelot's work

ideas.what: Hypercohomology of a complex of differential operators equals stratifying cohomology of a complex of stratified modules
ideas.modern_name: Linearization lemma; L(Ω^•) resolves O_{X/S}; infinitesimal = de Rham comparison
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (likely); Berthelot–Ogus Thm 6.12-type statements

ideas.what: When the diagonal is a nilpotent immersion, stratification equals descent data and Q°(F) = f^*f_*F
ideas.modern_name: Descent data vs stratifications for radicial-type morphisms; Cartier-type descent

deep.surprise_reason: This is a lecture draft of the linearization construction, which became standard through Grothendieck's Crystals exposé and through Berthelot / Berthelot–Ogus. It is historically nice to see it emerge in December 1966, along with the explicit remark on the asymmetry it resolves. The nilpotent-diagonal special case is a small aside, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Final statement should be read as 'cohomologie stratifiante est la coh. zariskienne ordinaire de [F]'; the manuscript literally writes X, a slip.

Bottom lines (inserted above the text): 'de ces deux voies' and 'zariskienne ordinaire' are interlinear insertions; 'complexe convenable de faisceaux stratifiés' is plausible but the word read as 'convenable' is uncertain.
Insertion '(ou germes' above the struck text is uncertain; possibly '(ou plus généralement'.
